cause: A first-stage engine shut down seconds after liftoff.
lesson: Engines are the riskiest part of a rocket; flight-proven launchers have had most of these problems fixed.
ref: Game summary of common launch failure causes — verify (NFR-09)

cause: A structural part broke under the stress of the climb.
lesson: Small parts matter: SpaceX lost the CRS-7 cargo mission (2015) to a failed strut, and fixed it by testing every part.
Separation systems are tested again and again on the ground because they only get one chance in flight.
ref: Game summary of common launch failure causes — verify (NFR-09)

cause: The fairing didn't open, so the rocket was too heavy to reach orbit.
lesson: NASA lost the OCO (2009) and Glory (2011) satellites this way; fairing systems are now checked far more carefully.
ref: NASA OCO and Glory mishap investigation summaries

cause: The upper stage shut down early and left the spacecraft in an orbit that was too low.
lesson: Margin matters: a rocket flying close to its limits has no room for small problems.
ref: Game summary of common launch failure causes — verify (NFR-09)

cause: The spacecraft never separated from the rocket.
lesson: Even the last step of a launch needs testing; a stuck adapter can end a mission.
ref: Game summary of common launch failure causes — verify (NFR-09)
